intent: The field of a multiple-value Combobox, holding one chip per chosen value and the inline input that takes the query.
typical_uses: The field of a combobox that holds several values

dont_use_when.situation: A combobox that holds one value

invariants.text: While at least one value is chosen the container renders with role "toolbar", and the arrow keys move between its chips and the input.
The container shows the field's focus ring while focus is anywhere inside it, and its border and ring turn destructive with `aria-invalid="true"` on the container.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the container's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the container's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (empty for this part). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A multiple-value field anchoring its popup
good.code:
const anchor = useComboboxAnchor();
<Combobox multiple items={frameworks}>
  <ComboboxChips ref={anchor}>
    <ComboboxValue>
      {(values) => values.map((value) => <ComboboxChip key={value}>{value}</ComboboxChip>)}
    </ComboboxValue>
    <ComboboxChipsInput aria-label="Frameworks" placeholder="Add a framework" />
  </ComboboxChips>
  <ComboboxContent anchor={anchor}>
    <ComboboxEmpty>No frameworks found.</ComboboxEmpty>
    <ComboboxList>
      {(item) => <ComboboxItem key={item} value={item}>{item}</ComboboxItem>}
    </ComboboxList>
  </ComboboxContent>
</Combobox>

bad.title: The single-line field inside the chips
bad.why: ComboboxInput brings its own border, trailing buttons and wrapper, drawn as a field of its own inside the chips' field; the input that sits among the chips is ComboboxChipsInput.

render.description: TS: ReactElement<unknown, string | JSXElementConstructor<any>> | ComponentRenderFn<HTMLProps, ComboboxChipsState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the container's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.description: TS: CSSProperties | ((state: ComboboxChipsState) => CSSProperties | undefined) | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. style accepts a function of the container's state as well as a plain style object. Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (empty for this part). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through combobox.module.css, not through this.
